requirement_text.REQ-364:
Implements REQ-363's design artefact exactly — no new schema decisions here, this requirement is implementation of an already-validated design, matching this project's own CODE-DESIGNER-then-ELIXIR-DEV split for every other schema-bearing feature.

SCOPE: the `Letflow.Help` context module (naming follows this project's existing per-domain-context convention, e.g. `Letflow.Identity`, `Letflow.TenantProvisioning`) exposing: create a draft, update a draft, publish (draft -> live, sets confirmed_at), re-confirm (bumps confirmed_at on an already-live row without changing body — the explicit "I checked this, it's still accurate" action), and read (by screen_id + tenant prefix, or by process_definition_id). Every write path enforces REQ-363's sanitization rule from that design, not a weakened version of it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the tenant-facing authoring UI (REQ-365 for platform, a separate future requirement for the tenant admin UI itself — this requirement's acceptance criteria stop at a working, tested context module, callable from IEx/tests, not yet wired to any HTTP route or frontend component). Route/controller wiring, if this project's own API-surface convention wants a separate requirement for it (matching the pattern most REQ-027..030-style definition CRUD work already used), is a natural fast-follow, not bundled here — state explicitly in this requirement's close-out whether a route was added or deliberately deferred, rather than leaving it ambiguous.

task.description: Run SECURITY-REVIEWER's gate (rework round 2) against ELIXIR-DEV's AST-based sanitizer rework (step-03-elixir-dev-rework2.json), including its two self-flagged design deviations. Scope-test the diff against security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-9, independently reproduce earmark_parser's real behavior for the two flagged gaps, re-verify all five original bypass payloads still reject, and actively probe for new bypass classes the AST-based mechanism itself might introduce.
acceptance_criteria: Every applicable invariant (INV-1..INV-9) verdicted with the specific evidence checked
The two ELIXIR-DEV-flagged design deviations are independently reproduced against the real earmark_parser dependency, not trusted from the handoff
All five original bypass payloads re-verified rejected, no regression
Any new bypass found is reproduced directly against create_changeset/2 with the exact payload and code-path root cause named
A blocking test-infrastructure issue discovered along the way is reported, not silently worked around

result.summary:
RECONSTRUCTION NOTE: this handoff was originally written live during WF02-REQ364-20260917's security-review saga as ad-hoc, non-schema JSON (informal top-level keys such as req/at/result-as-bare-string instead of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2's real schema), the exact anti-pattern this session's own ISS-0692 precedent names. It has been rewritten into full schema conformance by a later ORCH session under §4.1's not_agent_attested mechanism. created_at/started_at/completed_at are all set to the file's own git-introducing-commit timestamp (`git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%aI --reverse -- `), the best-available real timestamp, NOT the original live dispatch/claim/completion times, which were never recorded in schema-legal fields on disk. All findings, quoted test counts, and verification detail below are migrated verbatim in substance from the original ad-hoc file; nothing was invented or paraphrased away. SCOPE TEST: APPLIES -- tenant-scoped migration (priv/repo/migrations/20260917000001_create_help_content.exs, guarded `if prefix() do`, registered in Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0), a new Ecto schema (lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex) whose every read/write in lib/letflow/help.ex passes `prefix: prefix` explicitly, and a write-path sanitizer guarding against stored content later rendered to users. INVARIANT ASSESSMENT: INV-1: APPLIES, PASS -- verified all three sub-checks: (a) every Repo call in lib/letflow/help.ex (insert/update/get/all, 8 call sites) passes `prefix: prefix` explicitly; (b) migration's `create table(..., prefix: prefix())` is inside `if prefix() do`, and is registered in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 (git diff confirms both halves present in the same commit); (c) no tenant_id column exists on help_content at all (mirrors process_definitions' no-intra-schema-tenant_id-column convention per its own moduledoc) -- not a caller-supplied-tenant_id defect since there is no such column to misuse. INV-2: NOT-APPLICABLE -- S4 not started, no HTTP route/controller in this requirement's scope (help.ex moduledoc states this explicitly). INV-3: NOT-APPLICABLE -- S5 not started. INV-4: APPLIES, PASS -- grepped lib/letflow/help.ex and lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex for System.get_env and hardcoded-secret-shaped literals: zero hits, no secret material touched by this change. INV-5: NOT-APPLICABLE -- S4 not started, no lookup-by-ID HTTP endpoint in this requirement's scope. INV-6: Meta-invariant -- this handoff is the proof artifact. INV-7: APPLIES, PASS -- grepped for Repo.query across the changed files: zero hits, all access via Ecto.Query/Repo.insert|update|get|all. INV-8: APPLIES, FAIL -- see blocker 3 below. INV-9: NOT-APPLICABLE -- no outbound HTTP request in this requirement's scope. VERIFICATION PERFORMED: earmark_parser behavior independently reproduced: Ran `EarmarkParser.as_ast/2` directly (mix run --no-start against the real 1.4.46 dep, matching decision 0036 and mix.lock) rather than trusting the handoff's prose. Confirmed both claimed gaps are real: (1) `"click
here
"` parses to a single literal-text "p" child with no verbatim node -- inline-mixed raw HTML is genuinely never tagged verbatim; a line-starting `"
here
"` by contrast IS tagged `%{verbatim: true}}`, confirming the claimed asymmetry. (2) `"[x](javascript:alert(1))"` resolves href to the literal, undecoded `"javascript:alert(1)"`, and `"[x](java\tscript:alert(1))"` resolves href with the tab intact -- both confirmed not auto-handled by the library. Five original bypass payloads reverified against the real create_changeset/2: all five now genuinely rejected: (1) reference-style link definition -- rejected; (2) angle-bracket-wrapped autolink `[x]()` -- rejected; (3) backslash-before-colon `[x](javascript\\:alert(1))` -- rejected; (4) decimal HTML entity `[x](javascript:alert(1))` -- rejected; (5) embedded tab `[x](java\tscript:alert(1))` and embedded control char via ` ` -- both rejected. Baseline plain `[x](javascript:alert(1))` also still rejected. BLOCKER 1 -- new bypass, case-sensitive numeric-entity decode: payload `[x](javascript:alert(1))` (uppercase X in the hex marker, valid per HTML5's numeric-character-reference grammar). Reproduced: Letflow.Help.HelpContent.create_changeset/2 on this body: valid? == true, errors == [] -- the javascript: payload is accepted and would be written live to help_content.body untouched. Root cause: help_content.ex:127's @numeric_entity_pattern is `~r/&#(x[0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+);/` -- the hex-form alternative hardcodes a literal lowercase `x`, with no `/i` flag and no `[xX]` alternative, even though decode_entity_code/1 (line 280) is itself written to accept both (`x in [?x, ?X]`) -- the capturing regex never gets the chance to hand it an uppercase form. Because decode_numeric_entities/1 fails to match `s` at all, the entity survives un-decoded into scheme_letters/1 (line 262), which downcases the whole pre-colon span (`"javascript"` -> `"javascript"`) BEFORE filtering to ASCII a-z -- the now-lowercased literal `x` marker character from the un-decoded entity syntax itself survives the a-z filter as a real letter, producing the extracted scheme `"javaxcript"` (extra `x` injected) instead of `"javascript"`. `"javaxcript"` is not in @disallowed_url_schemes, so unsafe_scheme?/1 returns false. Same bug class REVIEWER's step-03d determination already named: a check written against an assumed-normalized string, defeated by an encoding variant the check's own author didn't enumerate -- previously CommonMark-syntax variants (reference-style, angle-bracket), now an HTML5-entity-syntax variant (hex marker case). BLOCKER 2 -- new bypass, raw tag split across inline AST leaves: payloads `xy` and `` xy `` (tag's '<' lands in one plain-text leaf, '>' lands in the leaf after the **strong**/`code` node). Reproduced: both -- create_changeset/2 valid? == true, errors == []. Confirmed via EarmarkParser.as_ast/2 directly first: `[{"p", [], ["xy"], %{}}]` -- three children, and the raw tag's own '<' and '>' each live in a DIFFERENT string sibling. Root cause: help_content.ex:219's fallback `walk(text) when is_binary(text)` scans each plain-text AST leaf independently against @raw_html_tag_pattern (requires both a literal '<' and a literal '>' within the SAME leaf). walk/1's list clause (line 198) calls this per-child, never reassembling sibling text nodes before scanning. This defeats the exact mechanism blocker_1 of ELIXIR-DEV's own rework2 summary calls out as the fix for gap 1 (inline-mixed raw HTML) -- the fallback scan closes the case where earmark declines to produce a verbatim node, but only when the raw tag's angle brackets survive in one unbroken text run. BLOCKER 3 -- INV-8, bare-match crashes on realistic non-adversarial input: payloads 'some text with `unclosed code' (a single stray unmatched backtick) and an unclosed fenced code block. Reproduced: both raise `** (MatchError) no match of right hand side value: {:error, ast, [...]}` at help_content.ex:178, inside the anonymous fn passed to Ecto.Changeset.validate_change/3 -- propagates straight out of create_changeset/2 (and equally update_changeset/2), uncaught. Root cause: help_content.ex:178 is `{:ok, ast, _messages} = EarmarkParser.as_ast(value)`, a bare 3-tuple match assuming the :ok branch always fires; EarmarkParser.as_ast/2's own documented contract sets status to :error whenever ANY emitted message has severity :warning OR :error, not only for a genuinely-unparseable document. `value` here is directly the tenant-authored `:title`/`:body` field content -- exactly the input class INV-8 names. A tenant author who simply forgets a closing backtick while writing ordinary help text crashes the write path. NON-SECURITY FINDING (flagged for visibility, not a security invariant): test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's @expected_tenant_tables (42 entries, comment says '22 tables' -- stale even before this change) was never updated to add "help_content", so test/support/tenant_template.ex's template_self_check!/1 raises `TENANT_TEMPLATE_SELF_CHECK_FAILED table set mismatch: missing=[] extra=["help_content"]` before ANY test using the shared tenant template can run. Reproduced directly: it does not reach a single test in help_test.exs. Consequence: the rework2 handoff's claim 'mix test test/letflow/help_test.exs: 47 passed' is not currently reproducible -- this is a real defect independent of the three security blockers above and must also be fixed before this round can re-verify test results at all.

issues.description: @numeric_entity_pattern's hex branch hardcodes a lowercase 'x' with no /i flag, so an uppercase HTML5 numeric entity hex marker (s) survives un-decoded, downcases into a literal 'x' during scheme extraction, and produces 'javaxcript' -- not in @disallowed_url_schemes, so javascript: payloads using an uppercase hex entity marker are accepted and written live.

The plain-text fallback raw-HTML scan (walk/1's list clause) checks each AST sibling leaf independently against @raw_html_tag_pattern; a raw tag whose '<' and '>' land in different siblings (split by any inline construct such as **bold** or `code`) is never detected in either leaf alone.

help_content.ex:178's bare `{:ok, ast, _messages} = EarmarkParser.as_ast(value)` match crashes with a MatchError on realistic, non-adversarial tenant input (e.g. an unclosed inline backtick or fenced code block), violating INV-8's typed-result requirement for tenant-controlled input.

test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's @expected_tenant_tables was never updated to add "help_content", so the shared tenant-template self-check fails before any test in help_test.exs runs, making ELIXIR-DEV's claimed 47/47 result currently unreproducible.

result.next_action: Route back to ELIXIR-DEV (third rework round on the implementation, not a fourth design round -- the AST-based mechanism itself remains sound; these are implementation-level gaps): (1) make @numeric_entity_pattern's hex branch case-insensitive; (2) reassemble/concatenate adjacent unstructured AST leaves (bounded to the same parent's children, excluding code/pre content) before applying @raw_html_tag_pattern; (3) replace the bare EarmarkParser match with a case/with that treats the :error branch as a validation failure, not a crash; (4) add "help_content" to test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's @expected_tenant_tables.
